notes: H1461 גּוּב ("to dig") was requested as a separate hapax, but its sole occurrence (2Kgs.25.12) is the exact same word form as H3009's own occurrence (Jer.52.16) -- both spelled וּלְיֹגְבִֽים, in what are parallel/duplicate narrative passages. WLC's own lemma tagging splits this one word across the two Strong's numbers (both entries even share the identical usage gloss "husbandman"), rather than it being a genuine second root. Modeled as one root, primary H3009, with strong_alt: ["H1461"] -- the same suppletion-pair mechanism used for הלך/ילך and נוח/ינח, except here it documents a corpus tagging split of a single word rather than two historically distinct roots. No separate H1461 file was created. search_match includes "1461"/"h1461" (a deliberate departure from the הלך/ילך precedent, where the alt number isn't searchable) since a person searching H1461 is looking for exactly this word, not something distinguishable from H3009.
